model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activation patterns and first-token attention scores across five distinct gating configurations in a neural network, organized into five rows, each containing two subplots: one for “Massive Activation” (left) and one for “first token attention scores” (right). All subplots share a common horizontal axis labeled “Layer,” ranging from 0 to 25, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The vertical axes differ between the two column types: the left column plots “Max Activation Value” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1600 (with intervals of 200), while the right column plots “first token attention score” on a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0 (with intervals of 0.2). Each row compares three components: “attn_output” (solid green line), “attn_residual” (dashed red line), and “ffn_output” (solid blue line), as indicated in the legends. In Row 1 (Baseline), the “attn_output” and “ffn_output” lines show a sharp rise after layer 6, peaking near 1600, while “attn_residual” remains near zero; the attention score plot shows fluctuating values around a mean of 0.467. Row 2 (SDPA Gating) shows significantly reduced activation magnitudes, with “attn_output” and “ffn_output” peaking below 400 and “attn_residual” near zero; the attention score plot remains low with a mean of 0.048. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) exhibits moderate activations, with “attn_output” and “ffn_output” peaking around 350, and “attn_residual” showing a small peak near layer 20; the attention score plot fluctuates around a mean of 0.297. Row 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share) shows “attn_output” and “ffn_output” rising sharply after layer 6 to peaks near 500, while “attn_residual” remains low; the attention score plot fluctuates around a mean of 0.361. Row 5 (Reduced Sparsity via NS-sigmoid) mirrors Row 1, with “attn_output” and “ffn_output” peaking near 1600 after layer 6, and “attn_residual” near zero; the attention score plot fluctuates around a mean of 0.481. Each attention score subplot includes a horizontal dashed green line indicating the mean value for that configuration.

The x-axis for all plots is linear, ranging from 0 to 25, with major tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis on the left-column plots is linear, ranging from 0 to 1600 in Row 1, 0 to 400 in Row 2, 0 to 350 in Row 3, 0 to 500 in Row 4, and 0 to 1600 in Row 5, with tick intervals varying per plot. The y-axis on the right-column plots is linear, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in all rows, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. In each left plot, three lines are shown: “attn_output” (blue, solid line with circle markers), “attn_residual” (green, dashed line with square markers), and “ffn_output” (red, dash-dot line with triangle markers). In each right plot, a single blue solid line with circle markers represents the “first token attention score,” with a horizontal green dashed line indicating the mean value, labeled numerically in each plot (e.g., 0.467 in Row 1, 0.048 in Row 2, 0.297 in Row 3, 0.361 in Row 4, and 0.481 in Row 5). The attention score lines exhibit fluctuating patterns across layers, with no consistent trend across configurations.
model_annotations.English:
Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five distinct gating configurations, organized into five rows, each containing two line plots: one for “Massive Activation” on the left and one for “first token attention scores” on the right. The x-axis in all plots is labeled “Layer” and spans from 0 to 20, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis on the left column is labeled “Max Activation Value,” ranging from 0 to 1600 (with some plots scaled lower, e.g., 0–400 or 0–500), while the y-axis on the right column is labeled “first token attention score,” ranging from 0 to 1.2, with a horizontal dashed green line indicating the mean attention score for each plot.

Row 1 (Baseline): The left plot shows massive activations for “attn_output” (blue dashed line) and “ffn_output” (red solid line) spiking sharply after layer 6, peaking near 1600 at layer 10, then declining. “attn_residual” (green dotted) and “ffn_residual” (purple dash-dot) remain near zero. The right plot shows fluctuating attention scores for “first token attention score” (blue line), with mean 0.467, showing peaks around layers 10 and 18.

Row 2 (SDPA Gating): The left plot shows reduced activations: “attn_output” and “ffn_output” rise slowly, peaking around 350 at layer 20. Residuals remain near zero. The right plot shows attention scores near zero across all layers, with mean 0.048, indicating no attention sinks.

Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): The left plot shows activations similar to Row 2, with “ffn_output” peaking around 350 at layer 20, but “attn_residual” and “ffn_residual” now show small but nonzero values (~50–100) after layer 10. The right plot shows attention scores fluctuating with mean 0.297, indicating residual attention sinks.

Row 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share): The left plot shows “attn_output” and “ffn_output” peaking near 500 at layer 10, then declining; residuals remain near zero. The right plot shows attention scores fluctuating with mean 0.361, with peaks around layers 5, 10, and 15.

Row 5 (Reduced Sparsity via NS-sigmoid): The left plot shows activations resembling the baseline: “attn_output” and “ffn_output” spike after layer 6, peaking near 1600 at layer 10, then declining. Residuals remain near zero. The right plot shows attention scores fluctuating with mean 0.481, with peaks around layers 10 and 18, resembling the baseline attention sink pattern.
